title: Brucie Smashes the Commissioner as the Villain Rides a Five-Game Wave
dek: No Banner only HULK hung 134.4 on Sonny's Horse, Team Pillbert won its fifth straight, and the top of the Buckaroo Football League now looks like a two-man arms race with a trade between rivals stirring the pot.
body: Somewhere, a controller is safe tonight, because Ramon had nothing to be mad about. No Banner only HULK dropped 134.4 points on The Horse is Hea, flattening the commissioner 134.4 to 102.58 in the highest score of the week by a full 27 points. The guy who wasn't even sure he wanted to be in this league is now 5-1 with 829.4 points for, nearly 100 more than anyone else. Sonny built the website, and Brucie keeps using it to post box scores like this.

The damage came out of the backfield. Kenneth Walker III ran for 26.9 points against a 21.85 projection, and Christian McCaffrey added 26.2 against a 19.15 projection, giving HULK two running backs who combined for 53.1, more than half of what some teams scored total. Sonny's James Cook III did his part with 22.8, but when your opponent has two backs doing that, a good Bills performance just isn't enough. The commish also left Bryce Young's 19.84 on the bench, which would not have closed a 31.82-point gap but certainly would have made the scoreboard look less like a hostile audit.

Meanwhile, the bad guy keeps winning. Alan's Team Pillbert beat The fumblers 107.06 to 85.5 for its fifth straight victory, and Philly's title odds jumped from 15% to 27%, which is the biggest climb in the league and is exactly the kind of plot twist that makes the rest of the league want to throw popcorn at the screen. Randy, on the other hand, had a week to complain about legitimately: Derrick Henry gave him 4.5 points on a 17.6 projection, and Trevor Lawrence sat on his bench putting up 27.34. That is a 21-point loss with a 27-point quarterback in the dugout, and The fumblers have now dropped three straight to slip to 3-3.

Elsewhere, Kai reminded everyone why he is the most dangerous 2-4 team in the league. Dawgs beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 105.6 to 83.44 as a road underdog, with Malik Nabers torching his 14.6 projection for 22.5. Mekhi won comfortably despite Kyren Williams busting at 8.2 and despite leaving Tyler Shough's 26.96 on the bench, which tells you how much talent the waiver-wire king has stacked up. Zilgit got the rough end of the rookie lesson, as Bijan Robinson posted just 6.3 points against a 21.34 projection, the worst bust of the week. And Habib finally stopped the bleeding, beating JMoney 100.5 to 92.72 behind Drake Maye, a waiver add this week who promptly delivered 23.8 points. Jordan got a gem of his own from Bhayshul Tuten, who nearly doubled his 11.69 projection with 22.7, but the numbers guy is now 1-5 with playoff odds that round to exactly zero.

The standings have split into tiers. HULK and Team Pillbert sit at 5-1, and while Brucie still holds a 50% title chance, that number actually fell from 56% despite a blowout, because the villain's surge is eating into it. Sonny is 4-2 with 86% playoff odds but watched his title chances slide from 18% to 10%. The real fight is for the fourth seed: Randy holds the spot at 3-3 with 33% playoff odds, but Kaushal (41%) and Mekhi (36%) are rated more likely to make it from 2-4, thanks to better point totals and rosters. Zoe sits at 4% and Jordan at 0%, though eight weeks of regular season remain.

The headline move of the week was a trade between the commissioner and the villain, which is either a bold alliance or the first act of a heist movie. Sonny sent Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith to Alan for George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II. Sonny also dropped Jalen Hurts, added Jameson Williams and Pat Freiermuth, and swapped the Bears D/ST for the 49ers D/ST, which the Chicago crowd will absolutely be noting as further evidence that Boston has gotten to him. Alan churned hard too, dropping Tyreek Hill and Odell Beckham Jr. while adding Josh Jacobs, Brenton Strange, Dameon Pierce and Tank Dell.

Over on the waiver wire, Habibi was moving at Georgia-highway speeds: he added Drake Maye and dropped Sam Darnold, picked up Woody Marks and then dropped him for Tony Pollard, added the Chiefs D/ST and Juwan Johnson, and cut Rome Odunze. Zoe made the most on-brand move of the season by dropping Lamar Jackson and adding Jordan Love, a Packers quarterback for the league's lone Wisconsinite, surely prompting a groan from every Chicagoan in the group chat. Mekhi tinkered with a new defense and kicker, adding the Ravens D/ST and Dominic Zvada, while Randy grabbed the Rams D/ST and parted with kicker Brandon Aubrey. Randy dropping a player is about as close as he gets to making a trade, so we'll count it as personal growth.

Week 7 serves up some juicy matchups. Zoe gets the white-hot Team Pillbert, a chance for the rookie to play spoiler against the villain. Randy and Sonny meet with both teams coming off losses and Randy desperately needing to protect that fourth seed. Dawgs vs. Habibsters is a straight-up playoff elimination preview between two 2-4 teams with real upside, and Jordan gets the unenviable task of facing Brucie's 829-point juggernaut. JMoney has the numbers; he just needs them to add up to about 135.

social.author: HULK Smash Society
social.text: 134.4. Two running backs over 26. A 5-1 record. Brucie didn't even want to be here and now he's the final boss. Stay mad, Buckaroos.

social.author: Commissioner Watch
social.text: Sonny loses by 31, drops the Bears D/ST for the 49ers, and makes a trade with the league villain all in one week. Requesting a full investigation into the commissioner's office.

social.author: Pillbert Pep Squad
social.text: FIVE STRAIGHT. Title odds from 15% to 27%. Everybody wants to root against Philliberto, and nobody can actually beat him. Enjoy the villain era.

social.author: Bench Report Daily
social.text: Trevor Lawrence put up 27.34 on Randy's bench. Randy lost by 21.56. We'll let you do the math, though Randy will probably complain about it either way.

social.author: Waiver Wire Insider
social.text: Kai left 26.96 on his bench and still won by 22. Malik Nabers with 22.5. The 2-4 record is lying to you. Dawgs are coming.

social.author: Cheesehead Corner
social.text: Bijan gave us 6.3 points, but Z Squared answered by signing Jordan Love. A Wisconsin girl with a Packers QB in a league full of Chicagoans. The rivalry is ON.

social.author: Habibsters Booster Club
social.text: Picked up Drake Maye, he dropped 23.8, streak snapped. Habib working the waiver wire like he's late for a speed trap. The two-time champ is not done.

social.author: Fantasy Stats Desk
social.text: HULK's PF lead over the field is now 97.8 points. Also: HULK won by 31 and its title odds went DOWN 6 points. That's what a five-game Pillbert streak does to a model.

social.author: JMoney Number Crunchers
social.text: Bhayshul Tuten nearly doubled his projection and we still lost. Next up: the 829-point monster. The math says no. We're playing anyway.

bios.1: The defending champ is 4-2 with 86% playoff odds, but a 31-point beating from HULK knocked his title chances down to 10%. Sonny responded with a trade for George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II plus a pile of waiver moves, so the commissioner is clearly not going quietly.
bios.2: Randy is 3-3 and hanging onto the fourth seed, but three straight losses have dropped his playoff odds to 33%. Derrick Henry's 4.5-point dud and Trevor Lawrence's 27 bench points made Week 6 one he'll have plenty to say about.
bios.3: JMoney is 1-5 and sits at 0% playoff odds, even after Bhayshul Tuten nearly doubled his projection. With HULK up next, Jordan's season is now about spoiling someone else's run.
bios.4: Philly has won five straight to reach 5-1, and his title odds nearly doubled to 27% this week. He also swung a trade with the commissioner and reshaped the roster with Josh Jacobs, Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith, so the bad guy is reloading, not resting.
bios.5: Kai is 2-4 but just beat Zoe by 22 while leaving 26.96 on the bench, which says plenty about the depth he's built. Malik Nabers is heating up, and with 36% playoff odds the waiver-wire king is very much alive.
bios.6: The two-time champ snapped his slide with a win over Jordan, powered by fresh pickup Drake Maye's 23.8 points. At 2-4 but with 41% playoff odds, Habib is still racing to get back into the playoff picture.
bios.7: Brucie's juggernaut is 5-1 with a league-best 829.4 points for after hanging 134.4 on the commissioner. Kenneth Walker III and Christian McCaffrey are steamrolling defenses, and the only thing slowing HULK down is a title-odds model nervous about the villain.
bios.8: Zilgit's rookie season hit a bump with two straight losses and a 6.3-point dud from Bijan Robinson, leaving her at 2-4. She went to the waiver wire and came back with Jordan Love, and a matchup with the red-hot villain gives her a chance to play spoiler.
